accepted.title: A reasonable logic capturing polynomial time on unordered structures
accepted.text: Capturing Ptime means defining exactly the polynomial-time decidable isomorphism-invariant Boolean properties of finite relational structures, with no input order provided. Does there exist a logic with a decidable set of sentences and an effective compiler translating each sentence φ into an evaluation algorithm and a polynomial bounding its running time, such that every such Ptime property is defined by some sentence?

accepted.title: Rank-logic queries are definable in Choiceless Polynomial Time
accepted.text: Rank logic is inflationary fixed-point logic with counting and the uniform finite-field rank operator of Chapter 7, whose prime characteristic can be specified numerically in the formula. CPT is the source’s Choiceless Polynomial Time logic with counting, using hereditarily finite sets over the input atoms with polynomial bounds on running time and the number of active sets, and no arbitrary choice of an atom. Is every rank-logic-definable Boolean property of finite relational structures definable in CPT?

accepted.title: Fixed-point counting with witnessed choice and interpretations captures Ptime
accepted.text: Capturing Ptime means defining exactly the polynomial-time decidable isomorphism-invariant Boolean properties of finite relational structures, with no input order provided. Does IFPC+WSC+I capture Ptime? IFPC is inflationary fixed-point logic with counting; WSC permits choices from definable orbits certified by definable automorphisms; I permits evaluation of a subformula in the relational structure defined by an interpretation. Use the iterated operator closure of Chapter 6.

accepted.title: Rank-logic solvability for every fixed finite ring
accepted.text: Rank logic is inflationary fixed-point logic with counting and the uniform finite-field rank operator of Chapter 7, whose prime characteristic can be specified numerically in the formula. For every fixed finite ring R, is there a rank-logic sentence deciding solvability of Ax=b over R for finite linear systems? Rows and columns are unordered index sets and coefficient labels are relations for elements of R; the finite ring and its operations are fixed in the problem, rather than supplied as variable-size input.

excluded.title: CPT canonization for all bounded colour-class structures
excluded.text: CPT is the source’s Choiceless Polynomial Time logic with counting, using hereditarily finite sets over the input atoms with polynomial bounds on running time and the number of active sets, and no arbitrary choice of an atom. For every fixed bound k and finite relational vocabulary, does CPT define canonization of all source-coloured structures whose colour classes have size at most k? A canonization is an ordered copy isomorphic to the input, identical for isomorphic inputs. Colours and their class ordering are supplied in the source’s encoding; no order within a colour class or restriction on its automorphism group is assumed.
